analysis.investment_thesis: Avanti Feeds is India's dominant shrimp feed maker with a fortress balance sheet (zero debt, ROCE 24%), but at 31.7x P/E it is priced ahead of its modest 12-15% growth reality and inherently cyclical aquaculture exposure. A good business, but not at a great price — I would wait for a 20-25% correction before building meaningful conviction.
key_strengths: Zero debt balance sheet with INR 3,011 Cr equity and virtually no borrowings — exceptional capital safety
ROCE of 24% and net profit CAGR of 15% over 9 years with last-5Y EBITDA trend clearly expanding (INR 346→738 Cr)
Market leader in Indian shrimp feed with export reach across 8+ geographies, riding India's aquaculture growth story
key_risks: Inherent cyclicality — EBITDA swung from INR 708 Cr (2018) to 346 Cr (2022) due to shrimp disease outbreaks and feed price volatility
Promoter holding at 43.23% is below my 50% comfort floor — raises minority shareholder alignment concerns
Thin and volatile operating margins (11.57% currently; peaked ~20% in 2018) make earnings predictability difficult for long-hold conviction
red_flags: Other income of INR 166 Cr (FY25) contributes ~30% of net profit (INR 557 Cr) — core operating profitability is overstated without this investment income
OCF turned deeply negative in FY22 (−INR 212 Cr) vs. reported net profit of INR 245 Cr — cash conversion is unreliable across cycles
Promoter holding below 50% with no publicly stated rationale for the sub-control stake level
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Avanti Feeds is a well-run business in a niche India has global competitiveness in — shrimp aquaculture. The balance sheet is pristine (D/E essentially 0.00, reserves compounding from INR 1,390 Cr in 2020 to INR 2,997 Cr in 2025), ROCE at 24% is healthy, and the 9-year net profit CAGR of 15% is respectable. The FY25 recovery — EBITDA INR 738 Cr vs. 346 Cr trough in FY22 — confirms the underlying business quality. I like the capex discipline (CWIP low, CapEx INR 131-153 Cr/year) and strong FY25 FCF of INR 437 Cr.

However, at 31.7x trailing P/E I am being asked to pay a premium the earnings trajectory does not yet justify. Revenue CAGR of only 12.6% over 9 years is underwhelming for a 30x multiple. More worrying: INR 166 Cr of other income in FY25 (likely treasury/investment gains) flatters reported profits materially — strip this out and the underlying P/E is above 40x. The cyclicality is real: this sector goes through shrimp disease cycles roughly every 3-5 years, destroying margins without warning. I would admire this company at INR 1,100 (approximately 24x P/E), not at INR 1,473. Watch it, don't chase it.
